name: Latvia

findings.controller: United States Department of State (joint declaration)
findings.local_actor: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Latvia
findings.summary: Latvia's foreign minister and the US Secretary of State signed a joint 5G security declaration urging supplier evaluation on rule of law and foreign-government control, and transition away from untrusted suppliers through normal replacement cycles.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Latvia

findings.analyst_inference: Non-binding declaration, tier 1; names no vendor or country. Coded as US-pole alignment statement rather than a Huawei ban: no Latvian law or regulatory exclusion of Huawei was found. LSM (Jan 2021, citing a CHOICE think-tank report) judges Huawei 5G participation in Latvia very unlikely. Reviewer call: whether a non-binding declaration belongs in networks at all.

findings.summary: Bite Latvija's technical director said the operator would not suspend its Huawei partnership and would continue planning its 5G network with Huawei despite security concerns.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 1: a stated intention, not a contract. still_current left null: no explicit reversal found, but the May 2022 Ericsson sole-RAN deal for Bite (LVA-003) suggests Huawei did not become Bite's 5G RAN vendor. Huawei's actual installed role in Bite Latvija's legacy network is unconfirmed.

findings.summary: Bite Group chose Ericsson as sole nationwide radio access network supplier for Latvia and Lithuania for 2022-2028, with Ericsson continuing to supply core technology and 5G rollout starting in major cities.
findings.analyst_inference: Ericsson (Sweden) is the equipment vendor, so pole third. Tier 3 as a signed multi-year supply deal; value undisclosed. Developing Telecoms likely derives from the Ericsson release, limiting independence. Neither source says Ericsson replaced Huawei.

findings.summary: Tele2 selected Nokia as its 5G radio access network partner across Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania, making Nokia its key Baltic 5G vendor.
findings.analyst_inference: Nokia (Finland) is the equipment vendor, so pole third. Single opened source; value undisclosed. Article does not say Nokia replaced Huawei in Tele2's Baltic network.

findings.summary: LMT selected Nokia's 5G standalone core, plus Nokia interconnect routers for data-centre fabric, to enable new 5G services.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole third (Finnish vendor). Single opened source; value undisclosed. LMT's RAN vendor not established in sources read. Overlaps in scope with LVA-006, which may supersede parts of this core work.

findings.summary: LMT chose Ericsson to modernise its core network for nationwide 5G standalone, replacing legacy HLR/HSS with Ericsson UDM, moving IMS to Ericsson Cloud IMS and deploying Ericsson NFVI.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole third (Swedish vendor). Two opened S3 sources but no S1/S2, so not corroborated; both likely derive from an Ericsson release. Nasdaq page undated; date taken from Business News Today. Value undisclosed.

findings.controller: Delska (DEAC/DLC, part of Swiss Quaero European Infrastructure Fund II)
findings.summary: Delska launched its EU North Riga LV DC1 data centre, 10 MW expandable to 30 MW and designed for AI and high-performance computing, after investing over EUR 30 million; infrastructure being prepared for first clients.

sources.publisher: business.gov.lv (Investment and Development Agency of Latvia)

findings.analyst_inference: Pole is genuinely debatable: operator Delska is a Latvian-Lithuanian brand, but DEAC and DLC have belonged to the Swiss Quaero fund since 2020, so coded third on ultimate ownership. Reviewer call: domestic vs third. Tier 4: launched but no confirmed tenants. EUR value not converted.

findings.controller: EuroHPC Joint Undertaking / LUMI AI Factory consortium (Finland-led)
findings.summary: Latvia was selected to host an AI Factory Antenna (AIFA-LAT), led by Riga Technical University and linked to the Finland-led LUMI AI Factory, with an EUR 8.4 million 2026-2028 budget including EUR 3.98 million national co-funding.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Education and Science of Latvia

findings.analyst_inference: Antenna gives access to remote EU supercomputing (LUMI, Finland) rather than local hardware, so compute controller is EU (third). Tier 2: selection plus funded programme; partner MoU due mid-2026 not confirmed. Year inferred from the page ('this autumn', project 2026-2028) and lvportals URL; exact date unknown.

findings.summary: Latvian company Tilde released TildeOpen, a 30-billion-parameter open model for European languages, trained on Finland's LUMI supercomputer under a European Commission Large AI Grand Challenge award and published on Hugging Face.

sources.publisher: Research Latvia (Ministry of Education and Science)

findings.analyst_inference: Weights controlled by a Latvian firm, so domestic. Whether trained from scratch or on a foreign base is not stated in the opened source, so base_model null. Tier 4: released openly; government or at-scale adoption not established. Training compute was EU (LUMI).

findings.local_actor: Ministry of Economics; Ministry of Smart Administration and Regional Development; LIAA; State Digital Development Agency
findings.summary: Latvian ministries and agencies signed an MoU with Microsoft to use Azure AI services in public administration, starting with an AI pilot for LIAA project evaluation, and to support a planned National AI Centre.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Smart Administration and Regional Development

findings.analyst_inference: Non-binding MoU, tier 1; no value. Coded models (Azure AI services/Model as a Service); no specific model (e.g. OpenAI) named. Year from AmCham page; ministry page gave only 3 December.

silicon.null_reason: AI-factory and data-centre searches surfaced no accelerator purchases or export-licence reporting for Latvia; Delska launch mentions no GPUs

applications.null_reason: no dedicated search; no safe-city or PRC surveillance deployment surfaced in network or government-AI searches

research_gaps: Three searches (English, Latvian) found no Latvian government-device ban or formal restriction on DeepSeek, unlike Lithuania; confirm with CERT.LV or the Data State Inspectorate.
No Latvian law or regulator decision excluding Huawei/ZTE found; check the Electronic Communications Law amendments and any SPRK/NBS vendor-screening rules.
Was Huawei equipment present in Bite Latvija's or Tele2 Latvia's legacy RAN, and has it been removed?
Is TildeOpen used by Latvian government services, and was it trained from scratch?
Exact date of Latvia's AI Factory Antenna selection and whether the partner MoU was signed by mid-2026.
Applications layer unresearched: any Hikvision/Dahua municipal CCTV in Riga or other cities.
